summary: herdr publishes no quantitative performance results in its README, docs or CHANGELOG; CHANGELOG performance notes are qualitative, e.g. docs/next/CHANGELOG.md:294 'reducing read latency for TUI agents', with no number. It ships runnable profiling harnesses: `just bench-*` recipes that run ignored cargo tests (render scaling at 1, 15 and 50 workspaces or panes, terminal target lookup, BSP layout, retained graphics, external API bursts) and a release CPU smoke comparison against the previous stable binary. Its pre-release audit checklist asks maintainers to record the 1, 15 and 50-count median and p95 render results, and none of those results are committed to the repository.
result_focus_note: manual classification of published_results: outcome = does the tool do its job; engineering = speed of the software itself
